title: The Last Keeper
tagline: A lighthouse on an island the ferries stopped visiting.

facts.tomas_here: Tomas lives in the oil shed.
facts.leaving: A date is circled on the calendar.

cards.speaker: Ines, on the radio
cards.text: The radio crackles. A woman, Ines, on a fishing boat: "Is anyone still on that rock?"

a.label: Answer her
a.result: She laughs, relieved. The static softens around her voice.
a.later: Ines calls every evening now. She calls you 'the voice on the rock'.

b.label: Stay silent
b.result: The static fades. The boat's engine grows distant.
b.later: Ines stopped calling. Her boat passes without slowing.

cards.speaker: The shore
cards.text: A crate washes ashore: tinned food and a soaked letter addressed to the last keeper.

a.label: Read the letter
a.result: Ink bleeds, but enough remains. You sit with it a long time.
a.later: The letter was from the old keeper's daughter. She writes that she's coming in spring.

b.label: Burn it for warmth
b.result: The paper curls. The tins stack neatly beside the stove.
b.later: The food lasted the month. Nobody will ever know what the letter said.

cards.speaker: The lamp
cards.text: The lamp motor grinds. Fix it now in the storm, or wait for calm?

a.label: Climb up now
a.result: Rain needles your face. The motor catches on the third try.
a.later: The light held all night. A trawler made it home because of it.

b.label: Wait it out
b.result: You listen to the wind and hope the sea stays empty.
b.later: A trawler ran aground in the dark. Everyone lived, but the mainland noticed.

cards.speaker: Ines, on the radio
cards.text: Ines asks if her brother Tomas can hide here for a week. He owes money to the wrong people.

a.label: Let him come
a.result: She exhales like she'd been holding it. "He'll be quiet. I swear."
a.later: Tomas sleeps in the oil shed and fixes everything he touches.

b.label: Say no
b.later: Ines is polite on the radio now. Just polite.

cards.speaker: A stranger at the pier
cards.text: A boat moors without asking. A man, Tomas, begs to stay a week.

a.label: Let him stay
a.result: He nods once and carries a thin bag up the path.
a.later: Tomas turned out to be Ines's brother. She started calling to thank you.

b.label: Send him off
b.result: His boat turns. The wake flattens against the rocks.
b.later: You saw his boat again, heading for the mainland police dock.

cards.speaker: Mainland official
cards.text: A mainland official radios: the light is being automated. Apply to stay, or take a pension?

a.label: Fight to stay
a.result: You fill every form twice. Your hand cramps around the pen.
a.later: They granted one more year. The paperwork says 'provisional'.

b.label: Take the pension
b.result: They sound pleased. The channel goes quiet after.
b.later: A date is circled on the calendar. Your last day.

cards.speaker: The tower
cards.text: The tower paint is peeling. It was red in 1902.

a.label: Paint it red
a.result: Red returns under your brush, stubborn and bright.
a.later: Ships radio in just to say they like the red.

b.label: Keep it white
b.result: You scrape and seal. Clean. Correct. Quiet.
b.later: The inspector ticked every box and left without a word.

cards.speaker: The storm
cards.text: A storm cuts the radio. A boat's lights are out past the reef.

a.label: Row out with a lantern
a.result: Oars bite black water. The lantern swings like a second heart.
a.later: It was Ines. She tells everyone on the coast.

b.label: Keep the light steady
b.result: You stay with the lamp. Beam and beam and beam.
b.later: The boat found the channel by your light alone.

endings.text: The island has a Sunday market now. You're not a keeper any more, just a neighbour.
The mainland gives up on automation. The light is yours for as long as you want it.
One spring the ferry comes back. You watch it from the gallery and decide not to wave.
